claims.text: The initial precursor is an equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr blend containing TaH0.5, NbH, HfH2, TiH2, and ZrH2.
The initial oxygen content is sufficient to induce alpha-HCP formation under standard sintering conditions.
Excess TiH2 can act as a sacrificial oxygen getter in the HfNbTaTiZr precursor.
Reactive titanium released by TiH2 decomposition preferentially consumes dissolved oxygen and forms stable TiO2 or Ti-O clusters.
The five stated hydrides decompose sequentially during heating and thereby drive alloying.
An argon atmosphere containing less than 25 ppm oxygen is suitable for the proposed dehydrogenation and oxygen-scavenging process.
A heating rate of 10 K min^-1 is suitable for processing the hydride precursor blend.
A temperature of approximately 1000–1100 K is above the highest decomposition temperature of the listed hydrides and is an adequate homogenization or sintering temperature.
Rapid quenching at more than 10^4 K/s is required to retain the metastable beta-BCC phase.
Preferential oxidation of TiH2 produces TiO2 nanoparticles and transient oxygen vacancies that prevent oxygen dissolution in the BCC lattice.
Laser-based additive manufacturing of refractory high-entropy alloys can produce cooling rates in the 10^4–10^6 K/s range.
Rapid cooling kinetically traps a single BCC phase in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Porosity generated by hydride decomposition provides a high nucleation density that refines the grain structure.
The proposed process will produce a nearly fully dense microstructure with greater than 99% relative density.
Rapidly quenched HfNbTaTiZr will have a metastable single-phase beta-BCC structure.
The getter-treated alloy will contain a negligible alpha-HCP phase fraction.
The getter-treated, rapidly quenched alloy will have an average grain size below 10 micrometres.
The resulting alloy will exhibit yield strength and ductility comparable to rapidly solidified refractory high-entropy alloys.
A control without the TiH2 getter will form alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC or an alpha-HCP-dominated microstructure, with larger grains and lower ductility.
If the cooling rate is below 10^4 K/s, metastable beta-BCC will decompose into alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC or alpha-HCP.

contradictions.description: The precursor is described as equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, but adding a stoichiometric excess of TiH2 without compensating the other elemental amounts would make the processed alloy Ti-rich rather than equiatomic.

The specified process is furnace-like hydride decomposition and sintering followed by quenching, whereas the mechanism invokes rapid solidification inherent to laser melting. A solid-state quench and laser melt solidification are distinct thermal histories.
